source.title: Fully flexible analysis of behavioural sequences based on parametric survival models with frailties -- A tutorial

confidence_rationale: A methods tutorial proposing parametric survival models (hazard/frailty models) as a more flexible, statistically validated alternative to simple Markov-chain transition-probability analysis for behavioral sequence data -- directly answering the source thought's request for 'validated measures of sequence structure' and 'experimental designs more rigorous than those suggested here.' Rated mixed because the paper's own motivation is an implicit critique of the informal transition-counting approach the source thought's language (refuge->explore->refuge->explore) most naturally suggests: first-order Markov transition-probability description assumes memorylessness, an assumption the tutorial's own framing treats as often unrealistic for real behavioral sequences. Confidence moderate given the source is a specialist-journal tutorial rather than a widely-cited landmark, and full text could not be directly verified (paywalled; based on abstract/secondary sources).
failure_signatures: The tutorial's own motivating critique is that standard sequential analysis of behavior has been underused in part because simple Markov-chain description assumes the transition probability from the current state depends only on the current state (memorylessness) -- an assumption that is frequently unrealistic for behavior organized in longer chains or context-dependent sequences, meaning naive transition-probability counting (the implicit default suggested by the source thought's refuge/explore/food-seeking transition language) can misrepresent real sequential structure that has longer-range dependence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Parametric survival analysis with frailty terms can model the time-to-transition from one behavioral state to several candidate follow-up states, accommodating complex experimental designs and estimating relative hazards for different transition types -- offering, per the tutorial's framing, a way to 'revive' rigorous sequential analysis of behavior beyond simple Markov-chain transition counting, and to detect more subtle aspects of behavioral organization than aggregate transition frequencies alone.
mapping.ree_translation: The source thought's language of transitions among refuge, exploration, food-seeking, acquisition, and return states implicitly suggests a Markov-chain-style transition-count analysis. This paper is direct evidence that a more statistically rigorous, established alternative already exists in the ethology methods literature for exactly this kind of question -- one that additionally accounts for HOW LONG an organism persists in a state before transitioning (a hazard/time-to-event framing), not just which state follows which. This maps closely onto GOV-BEHADJ-1's own listed candidate metric 'persistence of directed movement,' and suggests a REE behavioural-adjudication skill's 'Measure' step should consider survival/hazard-model machinery rather than simple transition-frequency tables when characterizing sequence structure.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Full text of this tutorial could not be retrieved directly (publisher paywall); this entry is based on the abstract and independently corroborating secondary sources (search snippets, indexing services), not a first-hand read of the methods and worked examples. The paper's own worked examples are drawn from farm-animal behavioral datasets, not computational-agent trajectory data, so specific implementation guidance for REE would require independent adaptation.
mapping.source_context: Methods tutorial in a specialist ethology journal, illustrated with two example behavioral datasets, aimed at applied animal-behavior researchers wanting a more flexible alternative to simple sequential/Markov-chain analysis of behavioral state transitions.

confidence_components.notes: Peer-reviewed tutorial in a specialist (not top-tier general) ethology journal; methodologically sound based on available abstract/secondary-source description but full text unverified due to paywall, so this entry should be treated as directionally reliable rather than exhaustively checked.
